prior_importants.description: A nested package with no dependencies but with its own lockfile is refused on every merge, and the install the message names never clears it. It ran fine before this change.

When the nearest lockfile sits in an intermediate directory (a workspace rooted below the repo root), the code still looks only in the repo root's `node_modules` and tells the operator to install in that intermediate directory. That install can never clear the refusal. It also newly refuses a branch that used to pass.

findings.description: A nested package with its own yarn.lock and a committed Yarn Plug'n'Play runtime (Yarn Berry zero-install) has no node_modules by design. Before this PR its stages ran and it merged. Now the gate refuses it on every attempt, and the install it suggests never creates a node_modules, so the refusal can never clear.
findings.body:
**A Yarn Plug'n'Play package is now refused on every merge, and the suggested install can never clear the refusal.**

`refuseUninstalled` treats "no `node_modules` anywhere" as "not installed". Plug'n'Play never creates a `node_modules`: packages resolve through `.pnp.cjs` from `.yarn/cache`, and a zero-install repo commits both. The project treats Plug'n'Play as supported. ADR 0143 (lines 107-112) says a `.pnp.*` repo only loses the diff-size split. ADR 0095 (lines 23-24) handles a Plug'n'Play install, and the adapter has `PNP_RUNTIME` handling (`typescript.adapter.ts:238-243`). No ceiling excludes nested Plug'n'Play packages.

**Trigger:** `tools/x` commits `package.json` with `devDependencies` and `test`/`typecheck` scripts, plus `yarn.lock`, `.pnp.cjs` and `.yarn/cache`. A session changes `tools/x/src/a.ts`.
- `touchedNestedPackages` resolves the package's manager to `yarn` (`typescript.adapter.ts:576-586`), so the commands are `yarn run test` and `yarn run typecheck`.
- Before this PR, `linkEnvironment` linked nothing. The stages ran in the checkout, Yarn loaded the committed `.pnp.cjs`, and the branch merged.
- At head, none of the early returns fire:
  - line 1671 finds no `node_modules` in the main checkout, and line 1672 finds none in the checkout;
  - `declared` is not empty;
  - `lock` is `{ dir: 'tools/x', manager: yarn }`, so `root === pkg.dir` and the hoisted check is skipped.
- The gate then throws "Install it with `yarn --cwd tools/x install`". That install still creates no `node_modules`, so every later merge that touches `tools/x` is refused the same way, and neither the operator nor the session can fix it.

The same path also catches a member of a root Plug'n'Play workspace (root `yarn.lock` and `.pnp.cjs`, no root `node_modules`). The hoisted check finds nothing under the root, and the advice names `yarn --cwd . install`, which doesn't help either.

(Medium confidence: the Yarn behaviour comes from knowledge of Yarn, not from reading its source in-tree.)

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/4428964be8cea8acdf5244120eb41aa57f2f5263/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L1680-L1698

**Fix:** skip the refusal when the nearest lockfile's directory holds a Plug'n'Play runtime in the checkout. The stages then resolve through it, as they did before this PR.

process_issues.description: Round 4 budget: spawned only correctness, security and guards. conventions, docs, simplicity, context and maintainability were skipped. spec had no source and workflow-safety had no workflow change. The consolidator was skipped because a single finding has nothing to group.
`gh pr diff 330` was denied for the guards reviewer. It fell back to `git diff <merge_base>..HEAD` on the service file and only searched the test file for source-scanning patterns.
